# M0-b-05: closing check of hardening round S1 (lane `check/M0-b-05-close-s1`, flow flow-7, stage group S, 2026-10-27)

The seat ran in a Claude Code cloud container: Opus 5.5, Linux x64, Node v24.12.0. The machine check
(`python3 tools/machine_profile.py --id`) printed `linux:Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.10GHz:4cpu:16gib`, which is the
id the brief names. `python3 tools/test_budget.py` printed **1** (and `--mutants` 1) before the runs, so every vitest
run used `--maxWorkers=1` and the mutants ran one at a time. The seat is an implementer-side closing checker (J162,
J169, J269), independent of the round: it is not the round's builder (`build/M0-b-05-fix-s1`, L-0669), the item's
author (`build/M0-b-05`, L-0295), its fix-round-1 author (L-0302) or an earlier checker (L-0300, L-0303). Its ledger
row is **L-0670** in `CLEAN-ROOM.md` §2. The lane log held no line for this lane key, so the seat started fresh
(no RESUME, no CONTINUE). This is the first part of **merged round M4** (M0-b-04 S3 follows and mirrors the two shared
shapes). The verdict file is this one, never `checks/M0-b-05.md`, which stays as the first check's (J269).

How the seat worked:

  (N10 – N13) in `checks/M0-b-05-notes.md`, its CLEAN-ROOM row, its two landed records and its lane-log lines. It ran
  **no git command** of any kind.

  `CLEAN-ROOM.md` L-0295, L-0302, **L-0669** — all permitted (M0.md §3 step 2). The round's changed sources are
  `verdicts.ts`, `tbars.ts`, `pool.ts`, `index.ts` and `flatten.ts`, its new test files
  `pool-exit-probe.ts` and `pool-exit-worker.ts`.
* **Mirror.** `/home/user/maps-scratch/waves/check-M0-b-05/close-s1/mirror/plat`, a `cp -a` of `plat/`
  (`find . -type l -lname '/home/user/maps-architecture*'` empty; the workspace links are relative —
  `bench/node_modules/@plat/layout` resolves inside the mirror). Unmutated baseline over `bench/test/bentcut-ng` at

  `/home/user/maps-scratch/waves/selfcheck-build-M0-b-05-fix-s1/` folder was never opened (it no longer exists).
* **Before-images.** No git command was run, so the seat holds no before-image of the round's files. In its place each

## Verdict: PASS

Every one of the round's seven rows is fixed (or carried / text) with a pin the seat re-killed itself; the two text-only
deliverables are in the tree. All gates are green, `landed:verify` passes for the item and its notes record, no export
was added, removed or renamed, no committed table, golden, digest, report or summary moved, and the refusal census did
not rise (lawful refusals 0 → 0 at both census sizes; 0 misses, 0 fall-backs). 31 targeted mutants: **26 killed**, 5
survivors — X2c and X2d **equivalent** (judged by this seat, with probe P2 as the receipt), X4e, X4h and X8b
test-tightness gaps whose code the seat's own probes confirm correct. No blocker; four new hardening notes
(N10 – N13, M4).

## (3) New findings, judged by the blocker rule

No blocker. A gate exits 0 everywhere; no listed interface or test id is missing; no stub or shortcut sits on an honest
path; no honest input gives a wrong result (the census's 189 + 60 runs and the two probes); no clean-room breach; no
path outside `plat/`. Four findings are notes in `checks/M0-b-05-notes.md` (M4 unless stated):

* **N10** — the 1 cm (`LATTICE.unitCm`) tolerance of `arcTangency`'s *spans* and *tangent* is unpinned: X4h (×50) and
  X4e (×100) survive the 9 test files, because the planted defects are gross (0.1 ℓ short, a straight chord) while the
  real arcs sit far inside the tolerance.
* **N11** — the applied line's pass-side literal (`; the run passes (exit 0)`) is asserted nowhere: X8b survives.
  Probe P1 shows the tree prints it, so this is a test gap, not a defect.
* **N12** — `tolBand`'s claim is wider than its reachable input: "an ⟨M-1⟩ cell with no row" cannot reach the
  no-single-row branch while `cut.sigma` and `cut.fillet` are `m1: false`, which is what makes X2c and X2d equivalent.
* **N13** — for the run items: the new `replay` gate fails a whole run when one district's replay batch fell back to
  S8's own run (`counts === null`, `replayed: false` — the over-limit path of `runFull`), which is lawful input, not a
  defect of ours; the row's other alternative (a bound on the missed share) is where M0-b-05a / M0-b-05b would go if
  M-1's faces produce one.
